LESSON: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we read widely?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency
2. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency
   In simple words: practise until you can read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment
   In simple words: practise until you can apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading.
4. Show that you can: read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Set up an after-school club where they meet on a regular basis and read varied texts,
2. Retell the stories they have read collaboratively,
3. Use materials in the classroom to read extensively,
4. Digital Literacy: This is developed as the learner uses selected reading materials from electronic sources.
5. Responsibility: This is cultivated as the learner engages diligently in assigned tasks on independent.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read widely?
2. What materials do you enjoy reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency
2. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
